title: Political Campaign
description: A chess-inspired strategy game where you run for office by positioning your campaign team across electoral districts. Deploy your Party Leader, Campaign Manager, Media Strategists, Pollsters, Lobbyists, and Volunteers to outmaneuver the opposition. Control swing states, dominate media markets, and build enough political capital to win the election.
learning_objectives: Develop strategic thinking by planning multi-step campaign maneuvers across districts
Practice resource allocation by deciding where to deploy limited campaign staff
Understand risk-reward tradeoffs when choosing between aggressive and defensive political tactics
Build spatial reasoning skills through positional control of key electoral territories
Learn adaptive decision-making by responding to the opponent's shifting campaign strategy
Cultivate long-term planning skills by balancing immediate gains against election-day positioning
how_to_play: Each turn you get 2 Action Points (AP). Moving a piece costs 1 AP, and using a special ability costs 1 AP.
Pieces move like chess: Leader=King, Manager=Queen, Media=Rook, Pollster=Bishop, Lobbyist=Knight, Volunteer=Pawn.
Capture enemy pieces by moving onto their square. Volunteers promote to Campaign Manager when reaching the last row.
Control resource tiles (Swing States, Media Markets, etc.) by placing your pieces on them. Each tile generates political capital per turn.
Win by: capturing the enemy Party Leader, controlling 3+ resource tiles, or reaching $10M in political capital.
Use each piece's unique abilities strategically — the Lobbyist's backroom deals and the Pollster's data-driven repositioning can turn the tide of any campaign.
objectives: Capture the rival Party Leader for an instant electoral victory
Control 3 or more key districts for a landslide resource domination win
Build your political capital to $10 million through strategic campaigning

storybook_pages.title: The Campaign Trail Begins
storybook_pages.text: Election season is here, and two rival campaigns face off in a battle for the hearts and minds of voters. Your team of strategists, media experts, and grassroots volunteers must outmaneuver the opposition across contested districts. Every move counts — the polls are razor-thin and victory belongs to the boldest campaign.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: two rival political campaign teams facing each other across a giant electoral map styled as a chess board, red and blue colors, dramatic spotlights, campaign banners and ballot boxes, digital illustration style

storybook_pages.title: Your Campaign Team
storybook_pages.text:
Party Leader (King) — Your candidate, protect at all costs.
Campaign Manager (Queen) — Most powerful, moves any direction.
Media Strategist (Rook) — Straight-line media blitz specialist.
Pollster (Bishop) — Diagonal data-driven analyst.
Lobbyist (Knight) — L-shaped backroom deal maker.
Volunteer (Pawn) — Grassroots power, promotes to Campaign Manager!
storybook_pages.image_prompt: diverse political campaign team members as chess pieces on a campaign stage, leader at podium as king, volunteer with clipboard as pawn, colorful modern illustration, game character design with political theme

storybook_pages.title: The Electoral Battlefield
storybook_pages.text: The 8x8 board represents contested electoral territory with 6 key districts: Swing States, Media Markets, Debate Stages, Rally Venues, Donor Networks, and Campaign HQs. Control them to generate political capital each turn and build your path to victory!
storybook_pages.image_prompt: birds eye view of a colorful 8x8 game board with glowing district tiles shaped like states, political themed with ballot boxes and microphones, campaign trail map style, digital game art

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.
